newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: PNG POLICE USE TEAR GAS

In Port Moresby, Police have used tear gas to disperse protestors and looters in demonstrations throughout the capital. A new protest is gathering outside Murray Barracks, the military main military centre and the focus of yesterday's main demonstration.

At the same time an Australian delegation, sent by Prime Minister John Howard and led by the Foreign Affairs Head, Phillip Flood, is meeting Papua New guinea Prime Minister, Sir Julius Chan, in an attempt to resolve the crisis.
PM SAYS AUSSIE NOT IN DANGER IN PNG
The Prime Minister, John Howard, says despite the volatile situation in Papua New Guinea, no Australians are in danger.
And Mr Howard has refused to be drawn on whether Australian troops will be sent to Bougainville as peacekeepers.
He's discussed a number of options with PNG Prime Minister, Sir Julius Chan, for the withdrawal of mercanaries from PNG, but has told ABC Radio he won't hamper the negotiations by revealing details.
On the security of Australians in PNG, the Prime Minister said the Australian High Commission is monitoring the situation closely.
GALES EXPECTED TOMORROW FROM JUSTIN
Gales are expected on the North Queensland coast tomorrow as Tropical Cyclone Justin again moves in from the Coral Sea.
The lastet report puts the centre of the cyclone 680 kilometres east northeast of Cooktown, and 730 kilometres north-northeast of Bowen.
It's moving southwest at 15 kilometres an hour.
Justin has been downgraded to a category 2, but still has wind gusts near the centre of up to 140 kilometres an hour.
AIR FORCE HOPEFUL SEARCH BY ORIONS WILL SUCCEED
The Air Force says it's hopeful a search by two Orion aircraft today will find five people missing in heavy weather on a yacht in the Coral Sea.
A search began for the "The Queen Charlotte" yesterday after a distress beacon was activated when the ship was believed to be about 100 kilometres from the centre of Cyclone Justin.
Squadron Leader Trevor Owens, from the Townsville RAAF base, says the standard search by the two P3C Orion aircraft should hopefully yield some results.
MAN IN WHITSUNDAYS FOUND SAFE AND WELL
A man whose boat broke down and drifted more than 40-kilometres overnight in rough seas in the Whitsundays, has been found safe and well.
The 32-year-old Club Med staff member got into trouble between Lindeman and Shaw islands .
Two helicopters and a plane had been searching the area.
Sergeant Mike Saunders says he was found by the Whitsunday Water Taxi drifting near South Molle Island, about 25 nautical miles from where he went missing.
FATALITY IN TANDEM THRUST
In central Queensland, there's been a fatality in the joint miltary exercise, Tandem Thrust.

An Australia Army Officer was killed in an accident in the Shoalwater Bay training area, around half-past-one this morning. A Defence Force spokesman says the man was riding an armoured personnel carrier near the Williamson airfield, when there was an accident involving the vehicle's hatch.
The officer was given prompt medical attention but died three hours later.
KENNETT UNDER FIRE FOR "GIRLS" COMMENT
Victoria's Premier, Mr.Kennett, is under fire for his reference, in State Parliament yesterday, to two of his opponents as "girls".
The Premier called Labor's John Brumby and John Thwaites "the two girls from Melbourne Grammar", and later said, "if you can't get a girl, get a Grammar boy".
The Principal of Melbourne Girls Grammar School, Christine Briggs, says the Premier's remarks were sexist and deplorable.
OPPOSITION PUSHING FOR SECOND REPORT INTO COLSTON
The Federal Opposition is pushing to have a second report into allegations against Independent Senator Mal Colston tabled in the Senate next Tuesday.
A Senate report into claims that Senator Colston misused his travel allowance is due to be tabled on Monday.
Labor's Senate leader, John Faulkner, will move to have the Administrative Services report, tabled as well.
Senator Faulkner says the motion would not apply if the Administrative Services Minister deems that publishing the report might affect current or potential police operations.
Senator Colston denies the allegations that he has misused his allowance.
